en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Wish-Fulfilling Wheel, in one fascicle.
Compiled by the Grand Master of the Household, Peer of the State, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Sui.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery—honored with a purple robe and the title of Minister of Works, posthumously titled Dajian (Great Mirror), and granted a fief of three thousand households—in accordance with the *Abhiṣeka-maṇḍala-sūtra*, by imperial decree.
I shall now expound the Dharma-gate of the *dhāraṇī* for those seeking swift liberation from the great ocean of birth and death;
one must first enter the consecration maṇḍala of the ocean-like assembly of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
Having received the empowerment,
one should give rise to a heart of joy and personally receive from the master the ritual rules for recitation.
Thereafter, in a pure chamber—
where mountain forests and flowing streams are most excellent—
one should establish a *maṇḍala* and install the principal deity.
The practitioner of the mantra should face the east.
He should smear the ground with *gomaya* (cow dung) and grind white sandalwood into fragrant paste.
Use it to smear the altar,
whether square or circular, according to one's preference as to its size;
then scatter various kinds of famous flowers upon the altar.
Offer incense and lamps.
Take two pure vessels, fill them completely with scented water,
and place them within the mandala for the purpose of making offerings.
Whether the practitioner bathes or does not bathe, there are no obstacles whatsoever.
One should simply direct the mind to contemplate and observe that the fundamental nature of all sentient beings is pure.
Being obscured by adventitious defilements,
one does not perceive the pure *dharmatā* of *tathatā*.
In order to bring about purification, [one practices].
One should, with a sincere mind, join the palms in the lotus gesture and recite this secret mantra:
Oṃ svabhāvaśuddhe hūṃ. By the power of the empowerment of this mantra, [the following occurs].
Having attained complete purity of body, speech, and mind,
one then places the five limbs upon the ground and pays homage with devotion to all Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions throughout the vast Mahāyāna.
Kneeling with the right knee on the ground, one should repent, rejoice, entreat [the Buddhas], and make vows, reciting this verse with a sincere mind at each instance:
I take refuge in the Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the ten directions, In the most supreme and wondrous Dharma, and in the assembly of Bodhisattvas;
With pure actions of body, speech, and mind, I reverently prostrate with palms joined in earnest devotion.
Whatever sins have been produced by the actions of body, speech, and mind throughout the beginningless cycle of existence within the various realms of being—
just as the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have confessed them, so do I now present my confession. Furthermore,
whatever merit has been produced through the three vajra-actions within the practices and aspirations of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas— [I rejoice in that].
I rejoice in all the roots of virtue accumulated by the Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, and sentient beings.

To all the Lamps of the World seated at the site of enlightenment, whose awakening-eye has blossomed to illuminate the three realms of existence, I now kneel and first entreat you: turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma.
To all Tathāgatas, lords of the three realms, who are about to enter parinirvāṇa without remainder,
I entreat you all to remain for a long time, not forsaking your compassionate vows to save the world.
Through the merit of this confession, sympathetic joy, and entreaty, may I never lose the bodhicitta.
Amidst the wondrous assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, you are always a virtuous friend, never wearying of or abandoning them;
born free from the eight difficulties, you possess the marks of wisdom regarding past lives to adorn your body;
far removed from delusion and confusion, you are endowed with compassion and wisdom, and are fully able to fulfill the pāramitās.
Born into noble lineages with abundant wealth and prosperity, With vast retinues that are ever-prosperous,
Possessing the four unhindered analytical knowledges and ten masteries, And fully perfected in the six supernormal powers and all dhyānas—
Just as with Vajradhvaja and Samantabhadra, May this dedication through praise be likewise.
Next, facing the principal deity,
sit in the full lotus posture or the half-lotus posture,
and give rise to a mind of great compassion.
I practice this dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, vowing to swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
First, grind various fragrances and use them to anoint my hands.
Then, one should bind the Samaya-dhāraṇī-mudrā of the Buddha Family:
join the two hands with palms hollowed and fingers interlaced,
then extend the two index fingers and bend them slightly.
Support the upper joints of the two middle fingers with the two thumbs bent,
and support the lower joints of the two index fingers.
The seal is then formed.
Place the seal at the heart and visualize the Tathāgata’s thirty-two major marks and eighty minor signs of excellence.
It will become clearly manifest as if facing it before one's eyes.
Recite this mantra seven times with a sincere mind. The mantra is:
Oṃ tathāgatodbhava svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the desired result is attained].
He immediately awakens all Tathāgatas,
who shall all protect, keep in mind, and empower the practitioner,
touching him with their light.
All karmic obstacles and hindrances shall be completely extinguished;
one's lifespan shall be long and far-reaching, and merit and wisdom shall increase.
The holy assemblies of the Buddha Family shall provide protection and rejoice.
In birth after birth, may they be free from all evil realms;
through lotus-birth, may they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Lotus Family.
Join the two hands with palms hollowed together;
extend the two index fingers, the two middle fingers, and the two ring fingers,
slightly bending them into the shape of a blooming lotus flower, and place them at the level of the heart.
Visualize yourself as the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, adorned with the primary and secondary marks of excellence and holding a sublime lotus flower.
Then, recite this mantra seven times and scatter it over the right side of your head, saying:
*Oṃ padmanābhāya svāhā*. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the rite is accomplished].
Immediately, he alerted Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the Holder of the Lotus,
and all the noble assemblies of the Lotus Family Bodhisattvas, who were all filled with joy, providing their empowerment,
protection, and mindful regard.
The light of all bodhisattvas shines upon and touches them,
whereby all karmic obstructions and hindrances are completely extinguished.
All bodhisattvas constantly serve as their virtuous friends.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Vajra Family:
turn the palm of the left hand outward and place the back of the right palm against it.
Place the back of the left hand [upon the right palm].
Use the thumbs and little fingers of both hands to hook them together,
forming the shape of a vajra.
Place it at the heart.
Visualize the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha holding a sublime vajra, possessing a majestic radiance and the marks of excellence.
Then recite the mantra seven times and scatter it from the left over the crown of the head. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vairocanābhāsaya svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the following occurs].
This immediately awakens all the noble Vajra assemblies,
who provide empowerment and protection;
all karmic obstructions and hindrances are entirely eliminated.
All sufferings shall ultimately not touch their bodies;
they shall attain a body as firm and unyielding as a vajra,
which no māras whatsoever can assail or disturb.
Next, perform the mudrā for protecting the body and donning the adamantine armor (*vajra-kavaca*).
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward,
pressing the right hand over the left.
Join the tips of the two middle fingers together and bend the two index fingers inward like hooks, ensuring they do not touch the backs of the middle fingers.
Then, place both thumbs side by side to press down upon the ring fingers; thus the mudrā is formed.
Empower one’s own body at five locations with the mudrā:
namely, the forehead, then the right shoulder, then the left shoulder, then the heart, and then the throat.
Finally, release the mudrā over the crown of the head.
Each shall recite the mantra once. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajrāṇi pratyāpadyasvāhā. Having bound this mudrā and recited the mantra, [proceed].
By means of this empowerment,
one becomes clad in the adamantine armor;
thus, all vināyakas and various celestial māras who create obstacles [are overcome].
They retreated and fled,
seeing that the practitioner’s body was enveloped in radiance and possessed sovereign majesty,
whether dwelling in mountain forests or in perilous places.
They shall all be entirely fearless.
All calamities such as water and fire, as well as every kind of misfortune— including tigers, wolves, lions, blades, staves,
shackles, and fetters— all such matters shall be completely extinguished.
Those who see it will rejoice;
after their lives end, they shall not fall into the evil realms,
but will instead be born in the pure and wondrous lands of the Buddhas.
Next, form the mudrā of the Vajrakīla for binding the boundary of the earth:
insert the right ring finger inside the left ring and little fingers;
insert the middle finger inside the tips of the left middle and index fingers, and do the same with the left hand.
The tips of all [the fingers] protrude outward,
with the tips of the remaining fingers touching one another.
One should then visualize the seal as having the form of a flaming vajra.
Place the thumb on the ground and pull it;
recite once for each pull, stopping at three.
Whether the area is large or small as desired, the moment you fix your mind upon it, the mantra for the solid earth boundary (*pṛthivī-maṇḍala*) is as follows:
Oṃ kili kili vajravārāhi huṃ phaṭ. Because one consecrates the boundary of the ground by forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the site is secured].
Downward to the water's edge, it is like a vajra throne;
neither celestial Māras nor various obstructors can cause harm,
and with little exertion of effort, one will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Next, form the mudrā of the Vajra Wall for the cardinal and intermediate directions.
This follows the previous earth-boundary mudrā,
with the exception that the two thumbs are opened and held upright.
The sides are shaped like a wall;
visualize the seal as being in the shape of a vajra.
Circumambulate the body three times to the right.
By setting the mind upon the Great or the Small [Vehicle],
one immediately forms a city as firm and solid as a vajra;
even the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not transgress it.
How much more so for all other beings who are difficult to subdue—
vināyakas and venomous creatures with sharp fangs and claws—
who do not assist those near the mantra. It says:
Oṃ sarā sarā vajraprakara hūṃ phaṭ. Next, the practitioner should visualize a great eight-petaled lotus flower in the center of the maṇḍala.
Above was a wondrous lion throne;
upon the throne was a pavilion made of the seven treasures,
from which hung various necklaces, silken streamers, banners, and canopies.
Rows of precious pillars hang with exquisite celestial garments;
clouds of incense spread everywhere, raining down various flowers while celestial music resounds.
There are precious vases and *argha* offerings, along with sublime celestial food and drink.
With mani-jewels as lamps.
Having performed this visualization, recite this verse:
By the power of my merit and by the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment...
"And by the power of the Dharma-realm, / I universally make offerings and abide.
Having spoken this verse,
he next binds the Great Ākāśagarbha Universal Offering Mudrā.
Join the two hands in *añjali*;
interlace the two middle fingers with the right pressing over the left on the outside,
and place them flat against the backs of the hands.
Place the two index fingers together,
curling them back toward the palm in the shape of a jewel.
Once the mudrā has been formed:
Recite the mantra four times.
The general offering mantra is:
Oṃ gaganasampravartaya vajra hūṃ. By the power of binding this mudrā and reciting this mantra as an empowerment, [the offering is accomplished].
Whatever offerings one intends to present are truly without distinction;
all the noble assembly shall partake of them.
Next, one should perform the mudrā of the precious chariot.
Interlace the two hands with palms facing upward;
cross the two index fingers so they touch each other horizontally,
and with the two thumbs, pinch the base of each index finger.
Visualize the seal as a chariot made of the seven treasures.
With the Vajra acting as the driver of the precious chariot,
one ascends into the void and proceeds to the World of Ultimate Bliss.
Request the assembly of noble ones to recite the mantra three times. The mantra is:
Oṃ tura tura hūṃ. By forming this mudrā and empowering it with this mantra, [the purpose is accomplished].
A carriage of the seven precious jewels arrives at that Land of Ultimate Bliss.
One should further imagine the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel, surrounded by a retinue of various holy assemblies.
Riding upon a precious chariot, he proceeds to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) and remains suspended in mid-air.
Next, one forms the seal for requesting the chariot.
Then, reciting the mantra for requesting the arrival [of the deity],
one draws the two index fingers toward oneself and flicks the two middle fingers.
First, recite the mantra three times as follows:
*Namaḥ siddhyādhyeśvarāya tathāgatānām oṃ vairocani-karisa-ye svāhā*. By means of the empowerment of this mantra and mudrā, [the rite is accomplished].
The assembly of noble ones has come from their own lands and dwells here in this empty maṇḍala. Next,
one forms the mudrā for inviting the samaya of the principal deity to descend into the maṇḍala.
Interlace the two hands within to form fists;
bend the left thumb into the palm and beckon it toward oneself with the right thumb.
Recite the mantra seven times. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ aruṇike acche acche svāhā. By the empowerment of this mantra and mudrā, because the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara does not transgress his original vow.
One should immediately proceed to the maṇḍala assembly to receive this offering.
Next, one should expel all obstructors by binding the mantra and mudrā of the Lotus Family Vidyārāja, Avalokiteśvara Hayagrīva Bodhisattva.
Join the two palms together and bend the two index fingers and ring fingers so that their nails face each other within the palms;
extend the two thumbs upright and apart.
Slightly bend the index fingers;
join and hold the two little fingers and the two middle fingers upright, one by one, and the seal is formed.
Reciting the mantra as you go, place it upon the crown of the head and rotate it three times to the left.
One should visualize the expulsion of all those who create obstacles and difficulties.
Upon seeing this seal, all māras will retreat and flee;
they will then immediately perform three circumambulations to the right. Thus it is accomplished.
The mantra of the Vidyārāja for binding the boundary is:
Oṃ amṛtodbhava hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, perform the mudrā of the Vajrapāśa net for the zenith.
Following the previous wall-seal,
join the two thumbs at the lower joints of the two index fingers.
Recite the mantra three times.
Place the mudrā upon the crown of the head and rotate it three times to the right. The mantra is:
Oṃ viśvara-narākṣa-vajra-panjara hūṃ phaṭ. By means of binding this mudrā and empowering it with this mantra, [the protection is established].
This immediately forms an indestructible net of adamantine solidity.
Next, bind the secret-sewing mudrā of the Adamantine Fire Court:
cover the back of the right hand with the left hand.
Raising both thumbs, recite the mantra three times.
Circumambulate the body three times to the right.
Visualize that outside the vajra wall, there are three layers of flames surrounding it. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ āsaṃmukhi hūṃ phaṭ. Next is the mantra and mudrā for offering the arghya perfumed water.
With both hands holding the vessel, offer it at the forehead.
Visualize the feet of the assembly of noble ones.
Recite the mantra three times; the mantra is:
*Namo samantabuddhānām āgaccha samayasambhava svāhā*. This is because of the offering of the *argha* perfumed water.
The practitioner attains purity of the three karmas and washes away the defilements of afflictions;
next, one should perform the mudrā for offering the lotus seat.
With both hands joined together with palms hollowed,
extend the ring fingers, middle fingers, and tips of the index fingers of both left and right hands,
bending them into the shape of a slightly opened lotus flower.
Within the precious pavilion, clearly distinguish all the noble ones and deities, each seated in their respective positions and surrounded by their retinues.
Recite the mantra three times; the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ kamala svāhā. By offering this with the empowerment of the mudrā of the lotus seat, the practitioner shall attain the fulfillment of the ten stages (daśabhūmi).
One shall then attain the Vajra-seat.
Next, form the seal of universal offering (*samantapūjā-mudrā*):
join the two palms with the ten fingers, placing the right over the left.
Interlocking the fingers as before, recite the mantra three times.

Visualize that from the mudrā there flow forth immeasurable and boundless oceans of clouds of scented unguents, oceans of clouds of flower garlands, oceans of clouds of burning incense, and oceans of clouds of food, drink, and lamps.
All shall become pure and vast offerings.
Then, recite the Universal Offering Mantra three times.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namo sarvatathāgatebhyo viśvamukhebhyaḥ | svāhā khaṃ ūnaṃ ti sa-phra hiṃ gagaṇa-kaṃ svāhā.* Next, one should recite verses of praise.

Kamalamukha (1), Kamalalocanā (2), Kamalasana (3), Kamalahastā (4), Kamalasumati (5), Kamalakamalā (6), Saṃsāramālā (7), Sāgarāmala (8), Kṣāranā (9), Namaste (10). One should then contemplate [them] accordingly.
Visualize [it] within one's own body, correctly at the center of the chest;
it has the shape of the full moon and its radiance is brilliant.
Upon the moon is an eight-petaled lotus flower.
Within the lotus womb there is a wish-fulfilling jewel,
red like crystal, its brilliant radiance illuminating immeasurable worlds.

Within that radiance, the principal deity, the Six-Armed Avalokiteśvara Cintāmaṇicakra, emerges, his physical marks and signs fully perfected, abiding in a meditative posture; having performed this visualization:
Arousing a heart of great compassion,
one should then form the fundamental mudrā of Cintamanicakra:
join the two palms together and bend the two index fingers into the shape of jewels.
Bend the two middle fingers so they touch at their tips like lotus petals;
join the two thumbs upright, and it is accomplished.
Visualize the deity as the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel Bodhisattva (Cintāmaṇicakra) as if clearly manifest before one's eyes, and then recite the root dhāraṇī seven times.
The mantra for the mudrā of scattering upon the crown is as follows:

*Namo ratnatrayāya, namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya, mahāsattvāya, mahākāruṇikāya, tadyathā, oṃ cakravarti-jñānamani mahāpraṇidhāna-rūpa-tiṣṭha jvala-ākarṣaya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* Next, perform the heart-mudrā of Cintāmaṇicakra.
Following the previous root mudrā, interlace the two ring fingers and the two little fingers with the right hand pressing over the left on the outside; this completes it.
Recite the heart mantra seven times and scatter [the mudrā] upon the crown of the head. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ bhadramantrijvala hūṃ. Next, form the heart-of-the-heart mudrā:
following the previous heart mudrā, cross the middle fingers outward.
The [mudrā] is formed by crossing and extending the little fingers.
Recite the Heart-to-Heart Mantra seven times and scatter it over the crown of the head;
the mantra is: Oṃ varadapradāne hūṃ. Then, take the rosary and coil it within the palms.
Consecrate [the rosary] seven times with the Heart-to-Heart Mantra (Cittacitta-mantra).
Then, holding the beads at the heart,
count them in succession while reciting until one hundred and eight repetitions are completed.
Alternatively, recite one thousand and eighty times while the mind abides in the samādhi of the deity;
do not allow other objects to intervene, but maintain perfect clarity and awareness of the number of recitations.
Place the jewel within the palm of your hand, then wear it upon your crown and restore it to its original position.
Thereafter, bind the three seals: the root seal, the heart seal, and the heart-center seal.
He immediately entered samādhi and observed that the luminous clarity of his mind gradually expanded,
pervading the entire dharma-realm;
he no longer perceived body or mind, having become the pure dharma-realm.
After a period of time as long as it takes to eat a meal,
he emerges from samādhi and next binds the seal of universal offering.
Offer incense, flowers, and so forth, as well as argha water;
perform praises and make aspirations;
then, form the mudrā for delimiting the fire enclosure and the boundary.
Turning once to the left above one's head constitutes the dissolution of the boundary (*sīmā-bandha*).
Next, form the chariot seal (*ratha-mudrā*) and sweep it outward.
Next, form the invitation seal (*āvāhana-mudrā*) and sweep it outward.
Next, having bound the protection-of-the-body mudrā and sealed the five locations,
one should next bind the samaya-mudrās of the three families and immediately exit the maṇḍala to walk about as one pleases.
One should recite Mahāyāna sūtras to dedicate the merit toward the attainment of the superior, middling, or inferior siddhis sought within the mind.
If a practitioner can recite this according to these instructions three times every day,
their karmic obstructions will be extinguished and they will attain great wisdom.
Through the accomplishment of samādhi, the deity will manifest before them, and they will obtain merits as described in the sūtra.
The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Wish-Fulfilling Wheel, in one fascicle.
